emt.label: EMT Student / New EMT
emt.summary: Assessment, communication, documentation, operations and first-year field habits.
guide: Assessment
Primary assessment, focused history/exam, vital trends and reassessment.
Communication
Consent, patient questions, radio reports, handoffs and team communication.
Documentation
Objective findings, timelines, response to treatment and local ePCR expectations.
Safety
Lifting, roadway/ambulance safety, PPE, equipment checks and fatigue.
Career
Certification and state licensure are separate; seek feedback and log de-identified skills.
cards: Primary assessment purpose?
Find and address immediate life threats while forming patient priority.
Why trend vitals?
Change over time may reveal deterioration, improvement or treatment response.
Strong handoff?
Problem, relevant history, key findings/trends, treatments, response and concerns.
Does NREMT alone authorize practice everywhere?
No. State licensure/certification and local authorization control.
What belongs in a skill log?
De-identified skill, repetitions, feedback and lessons—not PHI.
quiz: A patient looks worse although one vital is normal.
Ignore appearance
Use the whole assessment and trend findings
Document only the normal value
Use the complete patient picture and change over time.
Best way to improve a handoff?
Talk longer
Use a concise structure and get feedback
Skip trends
Relevance and structure matter more than length.

paramedic.label: Paramedic Student / New Paramedic
paramedic.summary: Disciplined ALS judgment: assessment first, medication/airway safety, ECG context, leadership and reassessment.
guide: Assessment first
Do not let the monitor or medication list replace a focused clinical assessment.
Airway
Positioning, ventilation, BVM, adjuncts, capnography concepts and reassessment.
Medication safety
Indication, contraindications, dose/concentration, route, effect and adverse response.
ECG context
Integrate rhythm/12-lead findings with symptoms, exam, vitals and serial change.
Leadership
Assign roles, communicate priorities, invite concerns and revise the plan when needed.
cards: What comes before an ALS procedure?
A clear problem, assessment, indication, risk/benefit and complication plan.
Why is BLS still central?
Assessment, ventilation, hemorrhage control, movement and communication remain foundational.
Medication reassessment loop?
Indication → safe administration → effect/adverse response → reassessment → updated plan.
Dangerous ECG habit?
Treating a machine label without integrating the patient context.
Good ALS leadership?
Clear priorities, role assignment, closed-loop communication and willingness to revise.
quiz: Monitor interpretation conflicts with the patient.
Treat the label only
Reassess tracing and patient in context
Ignore symptoms
ALS decisions integrate the whole clinical picture.
After medication administration?
Move on permanently
Reassess effect/adverse response
Assume it worked
Treatment belongs inside a reassessment loop.
